newsitem.title: DUBAI: Financials lead Oman stocks down in post-Eid trade.
newsitem.headline: Financials lead Oman stocks down in post-Eid trade.

text.p: Shares on the Oman stock exchange, led by finance sector stocks, slipped in the first week of trade after the Eid holiday in subdued trade.

The Muscat Securities Market, which reopened for three days of trading on April 21 after the Eid, said the index dropped to 273.18 points on Wednesday from 280.56 points on April 15, the last day of trade before the holiday.
This represents a 2.6 percent fall in the index.

The exchange said banking and investment shares dominated the market, accounting for 54 percent of trade. The services sector made up 24 percent, industrials 19 and the insurance sector three percent.

Al-Ahlia Portfolio was among the week's most active stocks, with 169,000 Al-Ahlia shares worth 1.25 million rials ($3.31 million) changing hands. The stock closed at 7.450 rials, down from 7.650 before the Eid.
Oman National Holding Company also closed lower, ending at 4.780 rials from 4.730 on April 15.
The total value of trade hovered around 7.47 million rials with 2.46 million shares traded.
